title: nwts: neutron weights of the three EPSR-test samples
purpose: Exercises `nwts`, the keyword-driven program that turns the isotopic composition of a sample into the neutron weights of every atom-type pair which `epsr` needs to compare its simulated partial structure factors with a measured differential cross section [@soper2005,@epsrmanual]. This case recomputes the three `.wts` files that the EPSR-test refinement actually uses, so it checks the standard single-sample path end to end.
fortran: `nwts.f`: `nwts` (component and isotope loop, exchange averaging, writing `<run>tot.wts`)
`process_symbols.f`: `check_symbol` (`symbol_setup.eq.'nwts'` branch: `fnameato` sets components, labels and symbols from the `.ato` file); `setup_symbols_generic.f`: `setup_symbols_nwts`
system: The EPSR-test mixture of 200 deuterated dimethyl sulphoxide and 400 water molecules (3200 atoms, 300 K, cubic box 33.12 Å) with six atom types: S, C, O and methyl H of DMSO, O1 and H1 of water. The three samples are d6-DMSO in D2O (H and H1 = 2H), d6-DMSO in H2O (H1 natural) and d6-DMSO in the null-scattering H2O/D2O mixture (H1 = 0.64 natural H + 0.36 2H), the isotope-substitution set of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992] measured on ISIS SANDALS. `nwts` looks up the bound coherent scattering length of each isotope [@sears1992], averages the abundances, replaces the lengths of exchangeable H1 by the mean over all exchangeable hydrogens, and writes for each pair the intra- and intermolecular products of concentrations and scattering lengths in the Faber-Ziman convention [@faberziman1965] (`output 1`: per atom, `normtot 0`: not normalised).
inputs: `200DMSO400Water.ato` and `DMSODWater{D,H,Null}.NWTS.dat` copied unchanged from EPSR-test (`nsamples 1`, `iexchange 1` for H1 only); `commands.txt` runs `nwts` once per file.
verification: The stored reference holds the three files the Fortran writes with new content, `DMSODWater{D,H,Null}.NWTStot.wts` (the rewritten `.NWTS.dat` and `.ato` files come out unchanged). These Fortran weights are themselves byte-identical to the `.NWTStot.wts` files shipped with EPSR-test (checked with `cmp`), so the port reproduces the weights used by the EPSR-test refinement, e.g. 0.0811 for S-S and 0.4417 for C-C of the null sample.
